title: What If You Swallowed a Watermelon Seed?

scenes.text: What if you swallowed a watermelon seed? The old warning says it sprouts. Your gut disagrees.
Within seconds it drops into your stomach, an acid bath that sits somewhere around pH 1.5 to 3.
In about six hours, it has ridden through your stomach and the whole length of your small intestine.
Your body keeps it near 98.6 degrees, inside the 70 to 105 degree range where watermelon seeds can sprout.
But for the next 36 to 48 hours it sits in your colon, a naturally low-oxygen place. Seeds need oxygen.
About two days after that bite, it simply leaves. The only thing that ever grew was the myth.

description:
What if you swallowed a watermelon seed? Food takes about six hours to pass through the stomach and small intestine, then up to 36-48 hours in the colon, according to Mayo Clinic.
Body temperature sits inside the range where watermelon seeds germinate, but seeds need oxygen to respire, and the large intestine is a naturally low-oxygen environment.
